title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1971-12-02

ai_review.summary: Mint soundboard capture of a smoking 71 show – Pigpen’s Smokestack Lightning, Keith‑filled jams and tight bandwork shine despite minor glitches.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid soundboard source with clear guitar, punchy kick drum and generally crisp mix; a few hums, feedback spots and a global channel swap are the only noticeable flaws. Musically the show is hailed as “smokes all the way through,” featuring standout Pigpen numbers (Smokestack Lightning, Turn On Your Love Light), a soaring Uncle John’s Band/Lovelight++ stretch and tight playing from the whole band, especially Keith on piano and Billy’s funky drumming.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and sound quality; minor technical issues are noted but do not detract from overall enjoyment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp guitar and kick‑drum mix, improved over earlier versions; occasional hum/feedback at the start and a global L/R channel swap noted by one reviewer. Overall clear and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows with a strong Pigpen‑centric first half and a seamless transition into tight jams; the band stays in the pocket throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar is higher in the mix, delivering impact on songs like Bertha and Casey Jones; side‑talk noted as entertaining.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as rich and fat (especially on “Truckin’/Tennessee”); overall solid foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm guitar sits prominently up front, adding drive to key numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano fills are praised for filling out the 71 sound and energizing the band.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy (Mickey) is called super‑funky on Love Light, sounding like a James Brown‑style groove; overall tight drumming despite minor channel swap.
